content: 1. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of ergotamine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base via the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Fosamprenavir also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Fosamprenavir reciprocally increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Co-administration of fosamprenavir with ethinyl estradiol may decrease amprenavir AUC, potentially leading to a loss of virologic response. Additionally, this combination may alter hormone levels. Alternative non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 7. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of everolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor patients closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. 10. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal fentanyl by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses accordingly. 11. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of transdermal fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. 12. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of transmucosal fentanyl by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses accordingly. 13. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects associated with CYP3A4 substrates. 14. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects; monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type symptoms. 15. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 16. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow dosage modification recommendations if adverse reactions occur. 17. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 18. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of imipramine by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Do not exceed itraconazole doses of 200 mg/day in patients receiving fosamprenavir/ritonavir. Dose reductions may be needed for itraconazole doses >400 mg/day in patients receiving fosamprenavir alone. 21. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. After discontinuing the inhibitor, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily. 22. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect. 23. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose reductions of ketoconazole may be needed for doses >400 mg/day. When co-administered with fosamprenavir/ritonavir, ketoconazole doses >200 mg/day are not recommended. 24. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 25. Levo-ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose reductions of ketoconazole may be needed for doses >400 mg/day. When co-administered with fosamprenavir/ritonavir, ketoconazole doses >200 mg/day are not recommended. 26. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of lidocaine by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of lofepramine by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates as per product labeling. 29. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Fosamprenavir may interfere with the manufacturing of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Discontinue antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period for elimination. 32. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of maprotiline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration may increase toxicity. Avoid during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 36. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of methylergonovine by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 37. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation due to higher systemic exposure. 39. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 40. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 43. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of nortriptyline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 46. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects emerge, further reduce to 50 mg/day. 47. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If no alternative exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 48. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose reduction of oxycodone may be warranted when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 49. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 51. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 52. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. 53. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. 54. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Decrease the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 55. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, decrease the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. 57. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of protriptyline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of quinidine by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 60. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. May increase creatine kinase levels.
